title: Past simple and past continuous
tagline: One action was already going on; another one just happened — telling a story means knowing which is which.
exam: Reading Part 4 — multiple choice on a long text
Listening Part 4 — true/false on a conversation
why: Reading Part 4 texts are often short stories or news reports, and Writing Part 2 asks you to write your own story — both need the past simple for events and the past continuous for the scene around them. B1 Preliminary rewards when/while/as used correctly to link two actions, and irregular past forms (went, fell, saw, heard) that examiners expect you to know by heart, not guess.

hook.text: Nadia: “My phone! I can't find it anywhere!” Liam: “We were walking to the bus stop when you opened your bag.” Sofia: “That's it — it probably fell out then!”
hook.ask: Two verbs describe things that were already happening; one verb describes the single moment something happened. Find them — which is which?

diagrams.title: The scene, and the moment something happened

marks.label: they were walking to the bus stop
the phone fell out of the bag

arrows: the shorter action cuts across the longer one
diagrams.caption: The past continuous paints the background; the past simple is the one thing that happened inside it.

diagrams.title: Build the sentence
diagrams.caption: Did carries the question and the negative in the simple form; was/were does the same job in the continuous.

rows.label: Use
cells: an action in progress around a past time — the background

rows.label: Time words
cells: yesterday, last week, in 2020, two hours ago
at six o'clock, all morning, while

rows.label: Linking word
cells: when + past simple = the sudden event
while / as + past continuous = the scene

rows.label: Example
cells: The phone fell out of the bag.

use.point: Past simple for finished actions and events

examples.text: The four friends met at the bus stop at half past five.
examples.note: an event that started and finished

use.point: Past continuous for the background of a story

examples.text: It was raining when they left school.
Sofia was talking to Miss Vega, so she wasn't watching the bags.
examples.note: an action in progress that explains what happened

examples.text: The friends were waiting for the bus for almost twenty minutes.

use.point: Two actions at the same time, or one interrupting the other

examples.text: While Nadia was looking for her keys, her phone fell out of her bag.
examples.note: while + past continuous, then the past simple interrupts

examples.text: Mateo was checking his messages when Liam shouted at him.
examples.note: when + past simple interrupts the longer action

examples.text: As they were leaving the shop, the alarm went off.
examples.note: as introduces the background action too

use.point: Irregular verbs and time expressions you need at B1

examples.text: They went back to the bus stop and found nothing.
Two hours later, Nadia rang her own number and heard it ring inside her bag!

watch_out.wrong: Yesterday I go to the cinema.
watch_out.why: A finished action needs the past simple, not the present.

watch_out.wrong: While I walked home, it started to rain.
watch_out.right: While I was walking home, it started to rain.
watch_out.why: The background, already-in-progress action needs the continuous after while.

watch_out.wrong: I was seeing Sofia at the market this morning.
watch_out.right: I saw Sofia at the market this morning.
watch_out.why: A single, complete meeting takes the past simple — see isn't normally used in the continuous.
Fall is irregular: fall → fell, never falled.

watch_out.wrong: When the phone was ringing, Nadia was answering it.
watch_out.why: Two short, complete actions one after the other both take the past simple.

watch_out.wrong: Did you went to the party?
watch_out.why: Did already shows the past, so the main verb stays in its base form.

l1.wrong: I go to the cinema yesterday.
l1.why: A finished past action always needs the past simple form in English, never the present.

l1.wrong: While I walked, it started to rain.
l1.right: While I was walking, it started to rain.
l1.why: Spanish mientras + imperfecto = English while + past continuous, the ongoing background action.
Regular -ed doesn't exist for irregular verbs like fall — you have to learn fell.

l1.wrong: Did you went to the party?
l1.why: Did already shows the past, so the main verb stays in its base form, not the past.

remember.trick: One thing WAS happening, one thing just happened!
remember.tip: Was/were + -ing paints the scene; the plain past tells the one thing that actually happened.

can_do: I can tell a story about something that happened, using the past simple for the events.
I can describe what was already happening in the background with the past continuous.
I can link two past actions with when, while and as, and use the key irregular verbs.
summary: Past simple = a finished action or event: regular -ed or an irregular form (went, fell, saw…).
Past continuous = was/were + -ing, an action already in progress around a past time.
When + past simple introduces the sudden event; while/as + past continuous sets the background scene.
Two short actions in sequence both take the past simple, even close together in time.
Learn irregular past forms one by one — there's no rule, only memory.
